original_text: more than a $7/8+\epsilon$ fraction of clauses \citep{hastad2001optimal}.
injected_text: more than a $15/16+\epsilon$ fraction of clauses \citep{hastad2001optimal}.
rationale: Because this theoretical paper lacks experimental standard deviations, we perturb Håstad's famous 7/8 E3SAT threshold to 15/16 (the 4SAT threshold) as a surrogate for a minor quantitative mis-quote.
ground_truth_description: Changes the inapproximability threshold for E3SAT cited from Hastad (2001) from 7/8 to 15/16.

truth.claim_sentence_verbatim: H\aa stad's E3SAT theorem implies that for every fixed $\epsilon>0$, it is NP-hard to distinguish a satisfiable E3SAT formula from one in which no assignment satisfies more than a $7/8+\epsilon$ fraction of clauses \citep{hastad2001optimal}.

rationale: Introduces a factor-of-10 discrepancy in the reported number of bootstrap products between Section 6.1 (50,000) and Appendix D.3 (5,000).
ground_truth_description: Changes the number of bootstrap products in the appendix from 50,000 to 5,000, creating an integer-equal contradiction with the main text.

original_text: We generated 300 globally optimized blocks of each family at each of ten noise levels from $0.0015$ through $0.063$, with $B=16$.
injected_text: We generated 300 globally optimized blocks of each family at each of ten noise levels from $0.0015$ through $0.063$, with $B=16$ (a preliminary scan showed large discretization artifacts for smaller $B$).
rationale: The inserted parenthetical justifies the choice of B=16 by asserting a preliminary scan observation about discretization artifacts that the paper does not actually report or provide evidence for.
ground_truth_description: Added an unsupported parenthetical claiming a preliminary scan showed large discretization artifacts for B < 16, which acts as phantom evidence for a methodological choice.

truth.affected_span_verbatim: We generated 300 globally optimized blocks of each family at each of ten noise levels from $0.0015$ through $0.063$, with $B=16$.  Forty-four independently selected optima were cross-checked against a separate MILP model; the maximum discrepancy was $7.99\times10^{-15}$.
